kurz: Sugar does more than sweeten. It keeps cakes moist, makes doughs tender, browns the crust and stabilises meringue.
bild_im_kopf: Like a sponge in the batter: it holds on to water and makes the cake dry out more slowly.
was_passiert: Sugar dissolves in the water in a batter and holds on to it. It slips between proteins and starch and so makes baked goods more tender. In the oven it browns the surface.
faustregeln: Cutting the sugar in a recipe too much makes cake dry and tough, not just less sweet.
Brown sugar holds more moisture: moister, softer cookies.

rolle.rolle: slows the gluten network, makes things tender
